newsitem.title: PERU: Suspected rebels attack Peruvian police, two dead.
newsitem.headline: Suspected rebels attack Peruvian police, two dead.

text.p: A group of suspected leftist guerrillas attacked a police pickup truck in the Peruvian capital on Sunday night and killed two officers driving inside, police said.

The attackers commandeered the pickup in the Huachipa neighbourhood on Lima's eastern outskirts, shot the two officers dead and threw their bodies into the cargo area of the truck, police at the scene told reporters.
"Judging from the way in which this attack was carried out, it does not seem to be the work of common criminals," a policeman on the scene told Reuters.

If confirmed as the work of guerrillas, it would be the most serious rebel attack reported in the capital since Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas overran the Japanese ambassador's house and took hostages on Dec. 17, 1996.
The attackers made off with rifles, bulletproof vests and a revolver which the police officers had been using, said police.
There was no immediate word on whether the attack was the work of the MRTA -- which continues to hold 72 hostages at the Japanese residence -- or another group, the Shining Path.
